title: The Gear Neighbors Turn Apart
premise: A toy machine wants two visible dials to rotate together, but directly meshed external gears turn in opposite directions. Adding a reviewed idealized idler changes the direction relationship and makes the transmission path visible.
hook: Why does the next wheel turn the other way?
visible_action: Two toothed disks mesh in close-up; a third idler slides between separated input and output gears and rotation arrows update.
intended_takeaway_or_theme: Each external-gear mesh reverses rotational direction in the idealized model.
gate: Verify gear placement and tooth contact; no powered-machine construction or pinch-point handling instructions.

style_application.why: Multiple angles expose a mesh that a single flattering view could hide.
style_application.check: Check tooth engagement, ratios, shared time and native/source reopening.

editorial_pick.original_reason: Meshing neighbors supply a compact visible mechanism that is also useful for testing synchronized rotation.
editorial_pick.proposed_first_version: Two large labeled gears first, then one additional gear. Use a clean diagram before considering a tactile 3D version.
editorial_pick.gate: Check tooth engagement, rotation direction and gear-ratio claims. A decorative mesh is insufficient.
editorial_pick.note: These are the catalogue's historical editorial recommendations, not current owner-approved selections or guaranteed watchable stories. Reapply the latest comedy/suspense gate.
